decisions.statement: A committed response is a 200.
A committed response is sent as an event stream.
A committed response tells caches to keep nothing.
A committed response is answered before the first attempt is made.
One keepalive comment goes out before anything else.
A keepalive comment goes out every 3500 milliseconds where no span is named.
A keepalive span of zero arms no heartbeat.
The hold is polled again every 2000 milliseconds where no span is named.
An attempt finding no account is followed by a wait and another attempt.
The observer slot is filled again before each wait.
A served status in the 200s is spliced through to the client.
A splice stops the heartbeat before the first upstream byte goes out.
A served status outside the 200s becomes an sse error frame.
The body of a served error is cancelled rather than sent on.
The error type a frame names is read off the status by `committed-outcome`.
An attempt that rejects sends an `api_error` frame.
An attempt that rejects ends the stream.
An attempt that rejects releases the hold.
An attempt that rejects stops the heartbeat.
An attempt that rejects is written about on the error seam.
A client that disconnects stops the heartbeat.
A client that disconnects releases the hold.
A client that disconnects cancels the upstream reader being spliced.
A heartbeat stopped by a disconnect re-arms itself never.
The stream is closed once however many ends are reached.
The hold is released once however many ends are reached.
A transport row is written only where the caller names a place for that row.
A transport row names the span the request was held before its splice.
A transport row has the reason the pool was empty.
A transport row is written once however many ends are reached.
An enqueue onto a closed stream closes the stream rather than throwing.
A caller hands in the attempt the hold is retrying.
A caller hands in the clock so a test needs no real time.
A caller hands in the sleep so a test needs no real wait.
A caller may hand in the timers so a test needs no real timer.
Nothing here chooses an account.
Nothing here forwards a request.
Nothing here reads a token.
Nothing here names the pipeline an attempt runs.
`tools/lib/model-gateway/committed-keepalive.ts` names the pipeline rather than taking a pipeline.
`tools/lib/model-gateway/committed-keepalive.ts` reads the clock directly.
Every line written here goes to the console rather than to a seam.
A splice that throws part-way sends no frame saying the stream broke.
A hold is bounded by nothing but the client hanging up.
The frames a splice sends on are counted nowhere in the transport row.

definition: the stream a client is held on while a request is still being tried
